Ways to work

As a team

Several people, several machines, one repository. The ledger shows who holds what, and a hand-off puts a blocker in front of the right person.

In plain words

When more than one person runs the loop, each loop needs to know what the others are doing, or two people will build the same goal. The ledger is a shared log on its own git branch: who claimed which goal, how it ended, notes, and hand-offs. A hand-off is how a loop says "this is blocked on something in your area" without parking into silence: it opens an issue assigned to the right person.

The ledger

QuestionAnswer
Turn it on"ledger": { "enabled": true } in .sdlc/config.json, then ask /sigma-ledger to set it up. Each teammate does the setup once in their own clone. /sigma-doctor sets it up if it is enabled but missing.
Where it livesA branch named sdlc-ledger, checked out as a worktree at .sdlc/ledger/. Pulling it never touches your working tree. The worktree must stay git-ignored so it never lands in a code pull request.
Why many filesEach writing process writes only its own entry file, so concurrent writers cannot conflict. The team view is their union, computed on read. Expect hundreds of files per person; that is the healthy state, and exactly one file for an actor means that actor's writes stopped.
Reading it/sigma-ledger shows what is addressed to you, a one-line team summary, and a regenerated TEAM.md rollup.
Writing itClaims and outcomes are written for you. You write by hand only for a note or a hand-off. A write you type publishes itself and says on stderr whether the team can see it yet.
FreshnessA background watcher pulls and publishes every 900 seconds by default and drops anything addressed to you into an inbox file.

Claims and leases

  • With the ledger on, a pick skips any goal another actor, or another live process of your own, already holds.
  • A claim with no later outcome is an open lease. It expires after 12 hours by default, so a crashed session cannot block the team forever.
  • A lease is advisory: it sees only claims already synced to the ledger branch. It is not a hard lock.
  • A session that ends or dies holding goals it never started has them released on the next pick, after a 15-minute grace; a started goal is never released.

Assignment and hand-offs

  • In GitHub mode the loop works only issues assigned to the person running it. Reassign by editing the issue.
  • When a goal is blocked on someone else's area, open a hand-off instead of parking: it creates an issue in their area, assigned to them, so their own loop picks it up.
  • They answer with one of accepted, deferred, declined or resolved. deferred does not settle it; the hand-off stays outstanding until resolved or declined.
  • Who a hand-off is addressed to comes from an ownership roster. It is advisory, and that is a choice; see the ownership guide.

Optional watchers

SettingDoesNeeds
agent_watch.enabledNotifies when a claimed goal's process is confirmed dead (email if configured, else a ledger note).ledger on
comment_watch.enabledNotifies the claimant of a new comment on a claimed issue.ledger on, GitHub source
ledger.autowatch.enabledDrives the loop on one flagged issue when a new item addressed to you arrives, after its preconditions pass.ledger on

All three are off by default. Each is opt-in and none starts without you turning it on.

Technical detail

Limits stated plainly. Two picks landing at the same instant with nothing yet claimed are covered only on one machine, by a POSIX file lock. That lock is unavailable on Windows, where the ledger's publish verbs refuse and defer unless you set an explicit override, accepting that two publishers in one checkout can then collide. Entry files are never compacted, so read cost grows with use; compaction is recorded as later work. A ledger problem never stops a run (every call fails open). Not measured beyond one adopter machine: behaviour with many active people. Sources: action log and ledger, area ownership.
